analysis.title: Weekly Warm-up: Enter Sandman
key_insights: MS US equity strategy (Wilson et al.) says the correction that began in June is in its final phase, with the S&P 500 catching down toward weaker breadth as breadth improves. Year-end S&P 500 base case remains 8000.

Since the end of September, 10-year Treasury yields have fallen nearly 40bp, the share of S&P 500 stocks above their 200-day moving average has risen about 20 points to 62%, and the equal-weight S&P 500 has gained nearly 5%, outperforming the cap-weighted index by almost 6%.

The equal-weight S&P 500 has outperformed the cap-weighted S&P and the Russell 2000 by 6% and 4% respectively since September. MS says the Russell 2000 likely needs a bigger decline in rates than seen so far, while the equal-weight S&P can work with a stabilization in the long end.

MS wants either further confirmation from its Market Sentiment Indicator (MSI, nearing capitulatory levels but not there yet) or the S&P 500 reaching its tactical downside target of 7100-7300 before adding risk more aggressively. A final capitulatory event is still possible.

Fed Chair Warsh acknowledged the tightening in financial conditions but distinguished between 'tighter' and 'tight'. He did not repeat his Jackson Hole message on getting inflation to target quickly. MS reads this as the Fed having flexibility to pause, with the bar for additional liquidity support still relatively high.

MS thinks liquidity may be tighter than the Fed acknowledged, so last week's FOMC was not a full clearing event for liquidity. This week's Quarterly Refunding Announcement is important, and less back-end issuance could help.

The Treasury General Account (TGA) has risen about $244B since mid-July while bank reserves fell $249B and Fed assets were essentially unchanged. Treasury projects a late-October TGA peak near $1.05T, falling toward about $850B by year-end, which could be a source of relief.

If the TGA drawdown does not coincide with less restrictive financial conditions across rate and energy markets, markets may need more liquidity from the Fed. MS asks whether the response would be orderly like last year or more disruptive like 2018.
Midterms are the most obvious clearing event. Since 1982, large caps gained about 15% (cap-weighted) and 16% (equal-weighted) in the six months after midterms, and about 22% over the following year.

A Democrat sweep via a narrow Senate majority is already anticipated by investors. A much more decisive Senate victory could push the market to look to 2028 for pushback against deregulation. Tariffs, foreign policy and agency-led deregulation remain largely under executive control.
MS sees the larger post-election risk as renewed military escalation with Iran or additional tariffs, particularly if higher energy prices push inflation expectations and long-end yields higher.

Recent pressure on the cap-weighted index came from the pace of AI capex, credit spread widening in parts of the AI trade, tighter liquidity, Middle East uncertainty and the midterms. MS views credit as becoming more discerning about issuance, not a broader credit problem. Hyperscaler supply is a small share of the market.

3Q26 earnings season favors quality. Free cash flow (FCF) surprises are driving larger next-day price reactions than EPS surprises, and FCF misses are penalized more heavily than usual. MS prefers companies with durable cash generation, strong balance sheets and improving revisions.
Industrials remains MS's top pick. MS favors higher-quality cyclicals that have de-rated, and sees crowded areas of the index possibly having more downside as part of the final capitulation.
60% of Russell 3000 stocks have seen at least a 20% correction since June, and the S&P 500 P/E multiple has fallen 20% from its high a year ago.
Early-cycle groups (Semiconductors, Capital Goods, Transports, Banks, Retailers) fell materially from their summer peaks, typical of a mid-cycle transition.

3Q26 earnings: median T+1 price reaction +0.1% absolute and +0.4% relative; EPS surprise 3.9% vs 4.4% historical average; sales surprise 2.0% vs 1.3% average. 297 of 493 S&P 500 companies (61% of market cap) had reported.
Consensus expects 3Q26 S&P 500 EPS growth of +28% y/y and sales +12%; calendar 2026/2027 EPS growth is 32%/16%. Earnings revision breadth is +7%, with slower upward revisions to 2027 this quarter.

Mag 7 earnings are expected to grow 25% in 3Q26 vs 22% for the S&P 493. For 2027 this flips to S&P 493 +17% vs Mag 7 +12%, largely on tough comps from one-off non-operating income. S&P 500 earnings have been skewed by unrealized gains on private AI investments.

MS systematic previews: net NTM EPS previews +21% (vs +27% last quarter) and net KPI previews +19% (vs +32%). Post-results net NTM EPS revisions across MS US coverage are +15% (vs +27% last quarter), with Real Estate (+56%) and Tech (+38%) strongest.
MS Fresh Money Buy List: 10 names including ABBV, AMT, CNP, DAL, EQT, KNX, NOC, TEAM, TGT, WMT, with average current-list return of 20.0% absolute and 9.39% relative to the S&P.

MS strategy forecast table: S&P 500 at 7,580 with scenario targets of 5,900 (bear, -22%), 8,300 (base, +9%) and 9,400 (bull, +24%). Sector overweights include Financials, Industrials, Consumer Discretionary Goods, Tech, Comm. Services, Health Care, Materials, Utilities; underweights are Staples and Real Estate.

tension_points.bull_case: Index catch-down toward improving breadth is the last phase of the correction; 10-year yields are down nearly 40bp, 60% of the Russell 3000 has already corrected 20%+, and clearing events (liquidity, midterms) should let earnings reassert as the driver toward an 8000 year-end S&P 500.
tension_points.bear_case: The MSI has not reached capitulation levels, liquidity may be tighter than the Fed acknowledged, a final capitulatory event is possible, and post-election Iran escalation or tariffs could lift energy, inflation expectations and long-end yields.
tension_points.what_invalidates: S&P 500 reaching the 7100-7300 tactical downside target, or the MSI hitting capitulatory levels, would be the confirmation points before adding risk more aggressively.
